elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM will: ..." — the trigger expressly covers both expiry and termination, for any reason, and the whole lettered set (a)-(c) hangs off that single trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months". The request condition is not tied to anticipated expiry only; it operates after every covered expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "... for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return all Content to Customer" — the 30-day clock runs from termination/expiry, not from a request. "Content" is the Agreement's defined term for Customer data (Sections 11.6, 14.18).

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "return all Content to Customer in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete all Content from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return, not on termination.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) provides up to six (6) months, which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Content within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination in a machine-readable format.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are carried by a single inserted sentence with correct temporal anchors (30 days measured from expiry/termination, deletion sequenced after return) and correct rate basis (then-current rates).

The insertion is a concise new paragraph for a genuinely missing clause; no existing words were deleted or paraphrased. The accrued-payment sentence in 3.5 and the survival list (which already names Section 3.5, so the new exit obligations survive without a bespoke survival tail) are untouched.

The extension to "or any Service Option Attachment" is justified by the Agreement's own partial-termination structure — Section 3.5's second sentence expressly contemplates termination of selected Service Option Attachments — so it is tailoring rather than a checklist extra.

No extras were bolted on: no at-own-expense language, no procedures, no additional damages or remedies, and no new defined terms; the insertion uses the Agreement's existing defined term "Content" for Customer data, leaving no dangling reference.
Intent preserved: unrelated allocation, payment timing and Service Option Attachment mechanics survive without contradiction, and no retained sentence conflicts with the new return/deletion duties.
Margin comment accurately states what changed and offers the 90-day/30-day fallback, consistent with the playbook tone.
